title: Concentric Gel System to Study the Biophysical Role of Matrix Microenvironment on 3D Cell Migration
protocol: Obtain MD-MBA-231 cells from the 37 °C, 5% CO2 incubator.
Detach cells from tissue culture plate using 0.5% Trypsin-EDTA solution.
Use 1 ml of Trypsin-EDTA solution for cell cultured in a T25 flask.
Pellet cells in a 15 ml conical tube by centrifugation at 200 × g for 4 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 5 ml of culture media.
Count cell density, ρ, using a hemocytometer.
Calculate the volume of medium required to achieve a 10× cell concentration.
Pellet cells one more time in a 15 ml conical tube by centrifugation at 200 × g for 4 min.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in the required amount (Vmedium calculated in step 1.3) of serum-free cell culture medium thoroughly to minimize cell clumping.
Obtain the stock collagen solution, 10× PBS buffer, Milli-Q H2O, and 0.1 M NaOH.
Keep all materials on ice to prevent premature polymerization of collagen.
Equilibrate a sterile glass-bottom dish by pre-warming it in a 37 °C incubator.
Calculate the volume needed for 50 µl of 2.4 mg/ml collagen solution.
Slowly add 5 μl of 10× PBS buffer to the calculated amount of collagen stock solution with gentle swirling.
Adjust the pH of the mixture to 7.4 using calibrated pH-meter and 0.1 M NaOH.
Adjust the pH of a collagen solution using NaOH and scale down volumes as necessary.
Confirm the final pH value using Litmus paper or micro pH electrode.
Bring the adjusted collagen solution to a volume of 45 µl using H2O.
Perform all steps on ice to prevent premature collagen polymerization.
Take the pre-warmed glass-bottom dish from the incubator.
Add 5 μl of the 10× concentrated cell suspension to solution I and resuspend thoroughly.
Add 20 μl of the cell-containing solution I slowly to the center of the well, forming a dome-shaped droplet.
Gently place the dish back in the incubator to let the inner gel polymerize for 45 min.
Prepare solution O (for the outer, acellular collagen gel) about 15 min before the end of this incubation step.
Calculate the required volume of collagen stock needed for 200 µl of collagen solution O at the final concentration.
Add 20 μl of 10× PBS buffer slowly to the calculated amount of collagen stock with gentle swirling.
Adjust the pH of the mixture to 7.4 using 0.1 M NaOH.
Bring the solution to a final volume of 200 µl using H2O.
Perform all steps on ice to prevent premature collagen polymerization.
Add 180 μl of solution O gently onto the inner gel without stirring, ensuring it completely covers the inner gel and fills up the well.
Avoid touching the inner gel with a pipette tip during this step.
Carefully remove any bubbles or air pockets that form.
Place the dish back in the incubator to let the outer gel polymerize.
Take the dish from the incubator after 45 min of polymerization.
Gently pour 2 ml of warmed cell culture medium into the dish.
Ensure the gel is completely submerged in the medium.
Refresh the medium every 2 to 3 days during the duration of culture.
Perform imaging using an inverted confocal microscope equipped with long-term live-cell imaging capability.
Warm up the microscope stage at least 1 hour before starting the experiment.
Incubate the gel in medium containing 5 µl of fluorescent cell tracker dye for 30 min.
Remove unbound dye by washing three times with 1× PBS.
Add cell culture medium to the dish after removing excess dye.
Take the dish from the incubator and place it on the microscope stage.
Select Volumes of View (VoV’s) in regions surrounding the inner gel for live-cell imaging after 24 hours of incubation.
Exclude regions closer than 50 µm from the bottom, side surfaces, and top of the gel to avoid edge effects.
Each VoV typically measures 647 × 647 × 100 µm3 (in x, y, and z directions) with a 5 µm interval in the z-stack.
Ensure imaging modes, channels/filters, exposure times, and image resolutions are correctly selected.
Use confocal reflectance microscopy for label-free imaging of the collagen network simultaneously during time-lapse live-cell imaging.
Take sample images and plot intensity histograms.
Adjust gains and offsets to observe sufficient signal and avoid saturation by ensuring the histogram lies between zero and maximum intensity.
Do not change these settings throughout the experiment duration.
Take time-lapse images of selected VoV’s with a 10-minute interval for 8 hours or longer if necessary.
Carry out quantitative image post-processing from z-stack images using appropriate software.
Segment time-lapse images to automatically select 3D cell positions in (x,y,z,t).
Manually check localization accuracy and remove false positives due to cell debris and cellular protrusions.
Remove proliferative cells from analysis.
Split overlapping or connected cells into distinct objects.
Generate 3D time-lapse cell tracks from the cell coordinates obtained.
Eliminate random and system noise by removing tracks shorter than a threshold track length, typically 20 minutes.
Correct for sample drift by subtracting overall net displacements from tracks if necessary.
Calculate cell displacement from observed cell trajectories.
Calculate cell migration distance from observed cell trajectories.
Calculate cell speed as S = d / (n • Δt), where Δt is the time interval between frames.
Calculate cell migration directionality using P = Δd/d.
